messages:
Olga S.: Quick idea — for Private/VPC egress, what do folks think about a small egress-operator that leases ephemeral IPs from shared pools and rotates duty every X minutes instead of per-tenant ENIs? I sketched tradeoffs below.

Kevin: Can you clarify the goal? Is this mostly for IP preservation (so long-lived sessions keep same src IP) or to save ENI cost?

Olga S.: Both. Main goals: 1) reduce per-tenant ENI count (cost/quotas), 2) give apps reasonably stable source IPs for upstream allowlists, 3) limit blast radius when an IP is abused by rotating duty. Operator would rebind IPs to different worker hosts on a duty cycle while trying to preserve affinity for warm flows.

Sasha: Sounds interesting. Two quick concerns: NAT table churn (SNAT mappings) and long TCP connections. If we rotate too aggressively we'll break long TCP. How do you plan to detect "warm" vs "cold" flows? :thinking:

Olga S.: Plan is heuristics + KV cache: track recent 5-tuple activity for an IP and extend lease if activity > threshold. Default leaseTTL=5m, extend on activity. For long TCP we can special-case connections with SYN seen earlier and avoid moving them until FIN/RST.

Ben: Need to think about IP exhaustion and burst. If shared pools run out, fallback should be per-tenant ENI allocation or fall back to existing NAT gateway. Also need rollout safety: we can't silently change public IPs for enterprise customers.

Deploy Bot: New RFC posted — https://rfc.local/egress-operator-draft (internal).

Maria: Observability asks: what metrics + events do we need? lease_count_by_pool, lease_churn_rate, allocations_failed, affinity_extensions, broken_connections_post_rotation. We should tie regressions to a customer-impact dashboard before enabling for Dedicated tenants.

Kevin: Ownership + permissions: operator will need permission to attach/detach IPs and modify routing/NAT. That increases blast radius. How do we make the operator auditable and reversible?

Sasha: Implementation idea: k8s operator with leader-election per-az. Each leader manages a set of IP pools and exposes a small RPC surface for allocating a sticky IP and for releasing it. Use tags/annotations for tenant mapping so we can query who had IP X at time T.

Olga S.: Example config I'm prototyping:
```
egressOperator:
  leaseTTL: 5m
  preserveAffinity: true
  warmThreshold: 20s
  maxIpsPerPool: 1200
  fallbackMode: per-tenant-eni
```

Ben: Rollout plan suggestion: internal infra-only first (no customer traffic), then opt-in alpha customers, canary with traffic shaping, and a global kill-switch. Also add audit log webhook and ability to pin IPs for specific tenants so we don't rotate for them.

Maria: For SLOs we should create a short experiment: enable on < 5% traffic and watch error rates + connection resets for 72h. Add a synthetic test that opens long-lived TCP to verify we don't regress.

Kevin: Edge case: what about on-prem/private deployments where attaching shared public IPs isn't allowed? Operator should support a local mode that just manages SNAT IPs inside the VPC or falls back to customer-managed NAT.

Sasha: Security note — operator credentials must be scoped and rotated automatically. Also create a read-only audit role so security can verify mappings without giving modify rights.

Olga S.: OK. Action items I took away: 1) update RFC with lease heuristics + pinning API, 2) add metrics list (Maria), 3) sketch rollout gates + kill-switch (Ben), 4) permission model + audit endpoints (Kevin/Sasha). Will add owners.

Ben: +1 to owners and runbook. Also please add a quick abort play for "mass connection resets".

Maria: I'll draft the dashboard and synthetic test.

Sasha: I'll prototype a leader-election sketch and label scheme for pools.

Olga S.: Thanks — I'll update RFC and ping infra team next week for a quick design review. :thumbsup:
